blurb:
A 73-pound golden retriever mix named Leo who is housetrained, good with other dogs, and described as high energy walked into a shelter and somehow nobody has scooped him up yet. That's the whole story. Someone is missing out.

Leo is four years old, which is a genuinely good age for a dog. Past the chaotic puppy phase, still plenty of years ahead, and already knows how to be a dog in a house. He gets along with other dogs, so if you've already got one, he'll probably fit right in. He's going to need real exercise — this is not a twice-around-the-block kind of dog — but if you've got the time and the energy for that, he's going to be an excellent companion for it.

His experience with kids is unknown, so if you have young children, a meet and greet first is the smart move. He's vaccinated, heartworm negative, neutered, and microchipped. Everything's already handled on the health side. Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville — walk in during visiting hours and ask for Leo.

blurb:
He came in as a stray with his tail tucked and his guard up. That's not a personality flaw — that's just what happens when a dog has been on his own and doesn't know yet if he can trust the people around him. His name is Hustler, he's a three-year-old pit bull mix, and the shelter staff will tell you that calm and gentle goes a long way with him. Treats help too.

Once he starts to trust you, he opens up. He's not a dog who needs constant stimulation or a packed schedule. Moderate activity level, steady temperament, just a guy who needed some time before he felt safe enough to show you who he actually is. Some dogs are like that. The ones who make you earn it usually turn out to be worth it.

He's not known to be interested in other dogs, so a quieter home without a pack would probably suit him best. If you've got patience and a calm environment, Hustler is fully vaccinated, heartworm negative, neutered, and microchipped — ready to go. Walk in during visiting hours and ask to spend some time with him. Bring treats.

Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville, TX.

blurb:
Monica came in from animal control, gained a few fans at the Mostly Mutts front desk pretty quickly, and is now working her way through the Prison Pups training program. She's about a year old, around 35 pounds, a hound mix, and her whole deal is being with her people. That's it. That's the whole thing.

She's friendly, gentle, and genuinely happy when she's around humans. The flip side of that is she does have separation anxiety, so a home where someone is around most of the day is going to make a big difference for her. Work from home? She would absolutely attend every Zoom call. She's also made friends with other dogs at the shelter, and having a calm dog companion at home might actually help her feel more settled when her people do have to leave.

She's heartworm positive right now, but treatment is coming and Mostly Mutts is handling it. Local adoption only while she goes through that process. A trainer from Mostly Mutts will also help her new family work through the separation anxiety piece, so you won't be figuring that out alone.

blurb:

blurb:
Someone found this little guy wandering around railroad tracks and had the good sense to stop. That's how Neo's story started. He's eight years old, about 15 pounds, a Bichon Poodle mix, and after a rough stretch that included a bout of pneumonia and a few weeks at animal control, he landed at Mostly Mutts and has been doing a whole lot better since.

He's a funny little guy when he's happy. Gets vocal about it. Rolls around on the floor being silly. Sometimes he wants to be in your lap, sometimes he just wants to sprawl out near you and look out the window. Either way, he wants to be close. He's currently in a foster home with a whole mix of dogs, from a Chihuahua to a Shepherd mix, and he gets along with all of them. He even worked out his feelings about the cats, mostly.

Neo does have ongoing medical needs and will require regular medication. That's real, and it matters. But he's stable, he's happy, and the right person is going to love taking care of this dog. He'd do best with older kids and a quieter home. If that's your situation, call Mostly Mutts and ask about him.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can reach them by phone or through their website to find out how to meet Neo.

blurb:

blurb:

blurb:
This guy has had a rougher run than most. Peeta was adopted as a kitten from Mostly Mutts years ago, returned when his family went through some life changes, adopted again, and then ended up back at the rescue after accidentally swallowing a string that required emergency surgery. He went through all of that and came out the other side still sweet, still affectionate, still winding himself around his foster's feet looking for attention. That says a lot about a cat.

He's about five and a half years old, around ten and a half pounds, and according to the people who know him best, he's as handsome as he is cuddly. He was shy when he first got back to his foster home, which makes complete sense given everything he's been through. But once he figured out he was safe, he opened right up. Now he actively seeks out affection instead of waiting for it to come to him.

Peeta is litter trained and got along with other cats in a previous home, so if you've already got a cat who could use a companion, he's worth a meet and greet. Kids are probably fine too, as long as they're gentle with him. He just needs a home that's going to stick around this time.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can find Peeta's full profile and reach out to start the adoption process through their website.
